findings.issue: Still open from the last review: at 1440 px both samples' running text spans about 790 px, about 95 characters a line ("Production and export sit within one company, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct"; the shortest sample runs as wide), and no change to src/styles/reference.css since then touches the intro.
findings.reference: The competitor's intro paragraphs are Maison Book 17/25.5 in a text column. Treatment-practice holds running text to about 70ch, so our measure follows our own rule, not the competitor's wider lines.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give the intro block's paragraphs (.block--intro p, or its text column) max-width: 70ch; leave the heading's width and its fit sizing alone.

findings.issue: The intro's heading is set in DM Sans 700, so at the fitted size of the longest sample ("Our Own Swimwear Factory in China", about 60 px) it reads as a heavy display title, much darker than the competitor's light heading in this module.
findings.reference: The competitor's heading+paragraph intro module ("Your Collection, Kept On Track", home 15) sets its heading large but in a light/book weight over a small blue uppercase eyebrow, so the heading leads the eye without weighing down the paragraph.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css lower the font-weight of the intro block's heading (.block--intro h2) to 500, and change neither its font-size nor the fit variables.

findings.issue: At 390 px the longest sample's heading ("Our Own Swimwear / Factory in China") is fitted to about 30-33 px, by its 32 px line spacing and the width of its lines, which looks at least as large as the home page's own H1 on phones (29.03 px in the manifest), so a section heading competes with its page's title.
findings.reference: On the competitor's phone pages the intro heading stays clearly below the hero title in size, so the page keeps one top level.
findings.fix: In the template's heading fit, cap a section heading's fitted size at the page title's computed size (for example clamp the fit result by a --title-size the template sets from the H1), so the intro heading on phones fits under 29 px on the home page; no site rule sets the size.

findings.issue: Each step title ('Scale and trial print', 'A4 approval options' …) is still set smaller than the regular text under it (about 3.7 px per character in the shot against about 4.1 px for the description), so the bold step names are outweighed by their own text. The last review's fix did not land and would not have worked: the title's size comes from the template's `.point-list__title { font-size: 1rem }` (patterns.css), not from --size-subheading.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each step name ('Custom Designs', 'Ready Designs', 'Mix n' Match') bold and clearly larger than the smaller body text under it.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give `.block--process .point-list__items[data-numbered] .point-list__title` a size one step above body text and below --size-card-heading, so it stays under the overview-steps lead, which is set at the card-heading size: e.g. change line 355 to `.block--process { --size-subheading: 1.25rem; }` and add `font-size: var(--size-subheading)` to that title rule. Keep font-weight 700.

findings.issue: On phones the step titles are still smaller than their descriptions ('Scale and trial print' is about 153 px wide for 21 bold characters; 'We send you digital mock-ups so' is about 263 px for 31 regular ones), so each description outweighs its step name. This also affects overview-steps ('Fabric on arrival', 'Cutting' …).
findings.reference: The competitor's step name is always the larger, bolder line above its text.
findings.fix: The same rule as on desktop: size `.block--process .point-list__title` from a .block--process --size-subheading above body size (about 1.25rem). It must not reach the root's 1.625rem mobile/desktop subheading value.

findings.issue: A step's title still sits right on top of its description ('Scale and trial print' / 'We send you digital mock-ups…'), with only the template's 0.25rem margin between them. This was reported before and is not fixed.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear gap of about 8–10 px between each step name and its description.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add `margin-bottom: 0.5rem` to `.block--process .point-list__items[data-numbered] .point-list__title`.

findings.issue: At 1440 px the step text still runs about 89 characters a line ('We send you digital mock-ups so you can approve the scale, and we turn strike-offs around'), over the 80ch limit for running text. This was reported before and is not fixed.
findings.reference: The competitor's step text keeps to about 65–75 characters a line.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `max-width: 70ch` on `.block--process .point-list__items[data-numbered] > .point-list__item > :not(.point-list__title)`.

findings.issue: Both numbered lists start on a hairline above step 01 but end on open space with no line under the last step (06 in m7, 05 in overview-steps), at both widths. This was reported before and is not fixed.
findings.reference: The competitor's list ends with a thin line under its last step ('Mix n' Match'), matching the line above the first.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add `border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary) 18%, transparent)` to `.block--process .point-list__items[data-numbered] > .point-list__item:last-child`.

findings.issue: The section still has no h2. Its lead 'Quality checks at every stage of an order' is now styled as a heading at the card-heading size, but on desktop it stands much smaller than m7's heading and only a little above the step titles, so the left column reads as a caption more than a section title.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list always opens with a real H2 ('3 Ways to Handover') over its lead, as m7 does with 'Mock-ups, Strike-offs and Sample Approval'.
findings.fix: Site Factory should supply a heading for overview-steps (e.g. 'Quality Checks at Every Stage') so the block renders its own h2 and the current sentence goes back to being the lead.

findings.issue: m7 and overview-steps are both numbered rows of short items under a heading on the left. They stand one under the other in exactly the same layout, so the second one reads as a repeat of the first.
findings.reference: The site's rule: when two sections of the same shape follow each other, the template sets one of them out as a list beside its heading. The competitor shows its process list once, not twice in a row.
findings.fix: Have the template use a different arrangement when two process:list blocks follow each other (e.g. the short-item one as a compact list without the large number column, or a horizontal steps row).

findings.issue: At 1440 px the check-list item text runs the full width of its column, out to the content's right edge, so lines reach about 95–100 characters (e.g. 'recycled polyester. Certified options are available on request, and your fabric determines which'); that is past the 80ch limit in treatment-practice.md and hard to follow back to the next line.
findings.reference: The competitor's running text keeps to a readable measure. The treatment practice holds running text to about 70ch at every width.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add a max-width of about 68ch to the item text in .block--icon-list .icon-list__item (the item's p), leaving the column and grid widths alone. m7 gets the same cap and stays as it is now, since its lines already end near 70ch.

findings.issue: The earlier finding is still open: each card's number ('01', '02', '03') sits on its own line above the title with a full line of space under it, so it reads as a separate label and adds a row to every card's head (on phones it is about 45px of the card before the title in both samples).
findings.reference: The competitor puts the number inside the bold card title, on the same line ('01. Custom Designs'), with the text straight under it (section-modules.json home 7).
findings.fix: In FeatureGridBlock.astro, for the outline-numbered pattern, render the number inside .feature-card__title as an inline prefix ('01. ') in the title's own type. Remove the separate number row from the card's subgrid (cardRows) and the matching [data-pattern="outline-numbered"] .feature-card__number rule in reference.css. The 'numbered' pattern keeps its large number on top.

findings.issue: The earlier finding is still open: there is little space between each card title and its text (about 10–20px at 1440, and the same in m2-3), so the title sits tight on the paragraph. reference.css still has no title-spacing rule for this pattern.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear gap under each card title before the text, about one and a half body lines (roughly 30–40px).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add margin-block-end: 1.25rem to [data-pattern="outline-numbered"] .feature-card__title (or set a matching row-gap on the card's subgrid).

findings.issue: The earlier measure finding is still open: the split copy's body paragraphs run about 80–87 characters a line at desktop (m4 'That cuts your development cost and your fit risk for a first collection. You can build' is 87; splitMedia-2 'Ask us for our design catalogue. Once you've sent your enquiry, we send you line' is 80). That is over treatment-practice's 70ch measure and its 80-character limit, because the only cap in reference.css is main[data-authoring-page] .block p { max-width: 70ch }, which in DM Sans renders about 87 characters.
findings.reference: The competitor's tinted split rows (home 2, home 12) keep their body copy to about 70–75 characters a line beside the media ('Swimwear Bali is a specialist custom swimwear manufacturer in Bali, making').
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, cap the split copy's paragraphs for every page, not only main[data-authoring-page]: .block--split .split__copy p { max-width: 58ch; } (about 72 rendered DM Sans characters; this covers m4 and splitMedia-2). Leave the copy column's width, its shared edge with the photo, its vertical centring and the heading's fitted size as they are.

findings.issue: The first paragraph ('Each sample costs USD 50…') is still set as a lead (about 20px on phones and a step larger on desktop), so on a phone it runs five large lines before the smaller body text starts; it is clearly bigger than the paragraphs under it and than the single paragraph in 'related'.
findings.reference: The competitor's split module sets every paragraph at one body size ('From seamless bikinis…' matches the text under it) and marks key points in bold, not with a larger first paragraph.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add .block--split { --size-lead: var(--size-body); } (or .block--split .block__lead { font-size: inherit; }) so a split row's first paragraph matches its body text; reference.css still has no split override (only .block--page-lead resets --size-lead).

findings.issue: Not fixed since the last review: the heading still sits on its own line above the brand row, so the section is a heading plus a strip under it rather than one band, which adds a heading's height to what the competitor sets as a single line.
findings.reference: The competitor's logo marquee is one row on white: the 'A FEW BRANDS WE PRODUCE' label sits on the content's left edge, on the same line as the marks, and the marks run on from it to the page's right edge.
findings.fix: Give the logos marquee a layout in the shared module that puts the heading at the start of the row, on the content's left edge and level with the marks, with the rail running to its right (stacked above the rail on phones). The heading keeps its template-fitted size; only its position changes.

findings.issue: The brand names are small bold caps about the size of body text, so the row reads as a line of captions under a large heading rather than a row of brand marks.
findings.reference: The competitor's marks are the row's main content: each one stands well above body-text size, with clear space around it, and nothing else in the row competes with them.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, make .logos-marquee .logos__name larger (e.g. clamp(1.125rem, 1.6vw, 1.5rem)) and keep .logos__note at its current size and muted colour, so the names read as the marks and the notes stay secondary. The row stays at rest and spread across the content while every name fits.

findings.issue: On phones only one quote card shows at a time, but the subgrid that lines up the cards' rules (reference.css:506-508) still sizes every slide to the tallest quote. The shortest sample's card has an empty band of about 80px between its five-line quote and the rule, and the attribution is pushed down with it.
findings.reference: The competitor's quote cards close a fixed space under each quote, followed by the bold name. No card carries an empty band inside it.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, apply the shared subgrid rows (.track__items grid-template-rows and .track__item / .testimonial grid-row: span 2; grid-template-rows: subgrid) only when every card is in view: add .track[data-fits] to those three selectors, or put them in a min-width media query. A slide shown alone then keeps its own height.

findings.issue: This repeats the earlier finding, which has not been repaired. A hard, dark 1px rule (figcaption border-top) still runs across every quote card between the quote and the attribution, at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor separates the quote from the bold name with space only, with no rule.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, set `.block--testimonials .testimonial figcaption { border-top: 0; }` and keep the subgrid row-gap (1rem) as the separation.

findings.issue: The same heading, "What buyers say", renders at two different sizes and apparent weights at both widths: it is smaller and lighter in the longest sample (/resort-wear-manufacturer/) and larger and bold in the shortest (/about-us/). A heading fitted to identical words should come out the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's testimonials heading is one consistent bold H2 wherever the module appears.
findings.fix: In the template's heading fit, check why the h2 on the /resort-wear-manufacturer/ sample gets a smaller fit size or lighter weight (for example, a cap from that page's title or a different heading level or class). Make the same words resolve to the same size and the 700 weight the manifest reports for h2.

findings.issue: The link-card labels are still 15px (template .related-links__link font-size: 0.9375rem; reference.css only changes their border colour). That is a step below the page's body text, so the cards read lighter than the section heading and the page's other link buttons at both widths. This was flagged in the last review and has not been repaired.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its title-case link buttons in Maison Book at 16px and its body text at 16-17px. None of its link labels is smaller than its body text.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add font-size: 1rem to the existing rule .block .related-pages--grid .related-links__link so the card labels match the body and button size. Leave the padding, hairline border, arrow colour and column count as they are.

findings.issue: The two-column FAQ still puts the heading in a left column beside a single column of questions, which leaves a blank band about 900 px tall under 'Frequently Asked Questions' on the longest sample. This was raised as P1 in the last review; it is lowered to P2 because the heading now sits on two lines instead of three.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ (home 16) puts its eyebrow and heading across the full content width, on a tinted band. The closed questions sit below in two side-by-side columns of hairline rows, each ending in a +.
findings.fix: Give the faq two-column variant a stacked layout. The heading spans the top from the content's left edge. Below it, .faq__items is a grid of hairline rows whose column count follows the question length: two columns when the questions fit, one when they are as long as these.

findings.issue: The open answer on the longest sample still runs the full width of the list column, about 90 characters a line ('Yes. Every year we make samples and bulk orders for more than 350 brands, and some of those'), so this 300-word answer is hard to follow from line to line. Raised in the last review and not fixed.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ rows sit in half-width columns, so their answers stay within a comfortable reading measure.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add max-width: 70ch to .block--faq:is([data-variant="two-column"], [data-variant="accordion"], [data-variant="open-list"]) .faq__item p (line 415). Leave the summary and h3 at full width so each question still runs up to its +/− mark.

findings.issue: The question list still has rules only under each row, so the first question ('Can you show examples…', 'Are any of your men's jammers…') has no line above it and the list has no top edge beside the heading. Raised in the last review and not fixed.
findings.reference: The competitor draws a hairline above the first row as well, so every question sits between two rules.
findings.fix: Add border-top: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary) 18%, transparent) to .block--faq:is([data-variant="two-column"], [data-variant="accordion"], [data-variant="open-list"]) .faq__items. If the rule should sit level with the heading's top, add the 1.25rem top padding back to the first summary (line 421).

findings.issue: On phones the list has no rule above the first question either, so 'Can you show examples…' and 'Are any of your men's jammers…' float under the heading, while every other question sits between two rules.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ opens its list with a hairline above the first row, at every width.
findings.fix: Use the same border-top on .block--faq[data-variant="two-column"] .faq__items without a media query, so phones get it too.

findings.issue: Flagged in the last review and still not fixed: in both samples the photo band stops about 20 px short of the screen edge on each side, so it looks like a boxed panel inside the content gutter rather than a closing band across the full width.
findings.reference: On home 17 the competitor's closing image band runs edge to edge across the 1440 px viewport with no side margin, and its copy keeps to the content's left edge.
findings.fix: In reference.css, make `.block--cta[data-variant="image-band"] .cta` full-bleed: `margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw); width: 100vw; border-radius: 0`. Keep the container gutter as the inline padding of `.cta__content` so the heading still starts on the content's left edge. The 1024px+ `--cta-copy-end` gradient then needs the same `max(0px, (100% - var(--container-max) - 2 * var(--gutter)) / 2) + var(--gutter)` offset that `.block--band` already uses.

findings.issue: Flagged in the last review and still not fixed: at 390 px the band is inset by the gutter on both sides and lines up with the FAQ list above it, so it reads as a dark card rather than a full-width photo band.
findings.reference: At 390 px the competitor's closing band fills the screen edge to edge.
findings.fix: Apply the same full-bleed rule to `.block--cta[data-variant="image-band"] .cta` at every width (`margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw); width: 100vw`) and keep the 1.25rem inset as the padding of `.cta__content`.

findings.issue: Flagged in the last review and still not fixed: in both samples the copy block is centred vertically in the band (longest: heading to button runs from about 29% to 70% of the band's height; shortest: about 30% to 72%), while the competitor's copy sits low in the band.
findings.reference: On home 17 the competitor's eyebrow, h2, paragraph and buttons run from about 43% to 83% of the band's height, leaving the upper part of the photo clear with the copy resting above the lower edge.
findings.fix: In reference.css at min-width 1024px, set `[data-variant="image-band"] .cta` to `align-items: flex-end` (or `align-self: end` on `.cta__content`) with `padding-block-end: clamp(3rem, 7vw, 6rem)`. Leave the min-height as it is.

findings.issue: Still the case, though better than before: in the longest sample the button label 'TALK TO US ABOUT SWIMWEAR PACKAGING & CUSTOM BRAND LABELS' still wraps to two centred lines even at the reduced 0.8125rem size. That turns the full-width pill into a tall slab, against reference.css's own aim of keeping the label on one line.
findings.reference: The competitor's band buttons carry one to three words each (BOOK A CALL-BACK, WHATSAPP, VISIT US, EMAIL US), so each stays a single-line pill on phones.
findings.fix: In Site Factory, shorten this CTA's button label to a few words (for example 'Request a label quote') and leave the topic to the heading.

findings.issue: The four cards are still white boxes with a 1px dark outline (repeat of the earlier finding: the fill rule at src/styles/reference.css line 297 only applies under main[data-page-type="solution"], so this /rash-guard-manufacturer/ sample keeps the outline).
findings.reference: The competitor modules this board is matched to (solution sections 2 and 7) use flat filled panels with a small radius and no outline: white or cream on a cream band, cream or light blue on navy. Only the home page's separate outlined trio uses a 1px border.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css widen the selector at line 297 from main[data-page-type="solution"] [data-variant="outlined"] .feature-card to every page type (e.g. .block--featureGrid[data-variant="outlined"] .feature-card { border-color: transparent; background: var(--surface-secondary); }), keeping --radius-card.

findings.issue: The two wide cards are still thin black outlines on white (repeat), so the short set reads as two mostly empty framed boxes. The fill rule limited to solution pages does not reach this /one-piece-swimsuit-manufacturer/ sample.
findings.reference: The competitor's two-card row ("Choose from 100,000 m in stock" / "Digital prints") is made of filled, rounded panels with no border.
findings.fix: The same change as for m2: apply the borderless var(--surface-secondary) fill to the featureGrid cards variant on every page type, not only under main[data-page-type="solution"].

findings.issue: On phones the card titles ("Performance fabric range", fixed at font-weight 700 by reference.css line 108) look bolder than the section heading "Rash Guard Fabrics, UPF Ratings and Certifications" and almost as large, so the step from section heading to card title is lost (repeat, not yet fixed).
findings.reference: The competitor's section heading ("Selecting Colours and adding Digital Prints") clearly outranks its card titles, which are smaller and no heavier.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set .feature-card__title to font-weight: var(--weight-heading) instead of a fixed 700, so card titles take the heading weight of their page type. Leave every font-size to the template.

findings.issue: The card title "Lightweight warm-water fabrics" breaks at its compound hyphen, leaving "Lightweight warm-" on one line and "water fabrics" on the next, at both widths. The other three titles in the row break between words.
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles ("Choose from 100,000 m in stock", "Digital prints") break only between words.
findings.fix: Site Factory: rephrase the title so it does not depend on the hyphenated compound (e.g. "Lightweight fabrics for warm water"), or join it with a non-breaking hyphen (U+2011) in the copy.

findings.issue: Not fixed since the last review: the heading 'Ready-to-Brand Curvy Collections and Low-MOQ Trend Drops' is still in regular weight, while the same module's heading in m2 ('Recycled Fabrics and Low-Impact Production') is bold 700, so one module shows two heading weights depending on how long its copy is. The phone shot shows the same.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one heading weight per level: its h2s are always in the bold heading face, and only the size follows the words.
findings.fix: In the bullets module's heading CSS (patterns.css, .point-list__intro h2 / the fitted section heading), hold font-weight at the h2 weight (700) at every fit step, so fitting changes only font-size and never the weight.

findings.issue: The intro (heading and lead) ends about a third of the way down a list roughly 1000 px tall and stays put, so the left column is an empty white band for most of the section's height while the points scroll past.
findings.reference: The competitor's long lists beside a heading keep the heading in sight next to the list. This site already does that for the process list's intro (.block--process .point-list__intro is sticky).
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, make the bullets intro sticky on wide screens as the process list's is: @media (min-width: 900px) { .point-list__intro { position: sticky; top: 6rem; align-self: start; } }.

findings.issue: Not fixed since the last review: with only two points, the list still runs as one column across the whole right track, so its lines run to about 90–95 characters ('Our low-MOQ, ready-to-brand trend drops let you test what sells in your market before you'). The 70ch cap in reference.css applies only to .block p and does not reach .point-list__item.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body copy beside a heading to short lines of about 60–75 characters.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, cap the point items' measure (e.g. .point-list__item { max-inline-size: 70ch; }) so lines stay short whatever the item count.

findings.issue: Still open after two reviews: at 390 px the four-column size table still runs past the right edge. The Weight column shows only 'We' and '12 / kg' clipped at the screen edge, and a faint shade is the only sign the table scrolls. Meanwhile the short cells wrap word by word ('About / 2 / years', 'Size / option'), so every row is three lines tall.
findings.reference: On the competitor's phone pages nothing is clipped at the edge; their facts read in full at the content width.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 600px): set .block--table .table-block :is(th, td) { padding-inline: 0.5rem } with :first-child { padding-inline-start: 0 }, and set white-space: nowrap on the short cells (td:not(:last-child), thead th). The four short columns then fit about 350 px and the last one wraps. If they still overflow, make the right-edge fade on .table-block__scroll[data-scroll="sideways"] wider and darker so the cut-off reads as a sideways scroll.

findings.issue: Still open: at 390 px the label column ('Detail') still takes about 40% of the table. That squeezes the spec column to about 20 characters a line, so rows run 6 to 15 lines ('Humid storage', 'Adhesive compatibility') and the 315-word table becomes a narrow strip about 1,900 px tall with empty space under every label.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone text runs the full content width at about 35–45 characters a line; it never packs prose into a column this narrow.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 600px), stack the two-column table: .block--table .table-block:not(:has(thead tr > :nth-child(3))) tr { display: block; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-table) } and its th, td { display: block; border: 0; padding-inline: 0 }. Make the first cell a bold label over a full-width text cell, and hide the thead visually. Keep the four-column m5 table as a table.

findings.issue: Still open: the 'Specification and consequence' column still runs about 100–115 characters a line ('Made from 90% recycled materials and available in 3 shapes: thong, standard bikini and full coverage. The water-'). The table still spans the whole content width of about 1,130 px, so .block--table .table-block__scroll { max-width: calc(70ch + 20rem) } is not taking effect.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body text to a short measure of about 60–75 characters a line.
findings.fix: Check that the max-width actually reaches the wrapper that sets the table's width; the table itself may be the element at width: 100% of the section. If it doesn't, cap the cells directly: .block--table .table-block table { inline-size: auto; max-inline-size: 100% } and .block--table .table-block td:last-child { max-inline-size: 70ch }. The text column then keeps about 70 characters beside the label column, starting at the heading's left edge.

findings.issue: Still open: the m5 heading ('Toddler Sizes and Custom Size Runs') is still set in a regular weight, while m9's table heading on the same board is bold DM Sans 700. Two headings of the same level show different weights, at 390 px as well.
findings.reference: The competitor sets every section h2 in one heavy weight throughout.
findings.fix: Set font-weight: 700 on .block--table h2 (the table block's heading, in every variant) to match the site's h2 weight, and leave its fitted size alone.

findings.issue: At 390 px the first cell of each row (and the header) is inset about 16 px from the content's left edge, so the labels 'Detail', 'Kraft paper' and 'Size option' start to the right of the heading and intro above them. Their row rules still start at the edge (m5 too).
findings.reference: The competitor starts its section text and facts on one left edge.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 600px): .block--table .table-block :is(th, td):first-child { padding-inline-start: 0 }.

findings.issue: On phones the quote button in both samples still fills the whole column (about 350 px) and reads as a heavy black bar under the copy, so the last review's P2 is not fixed yet. The fix takes the inline CTA out of the phone full-width button rule in reference.css, which an earlier finding added for the closing bands. That is needed here because the mobile shot shows the competitor's inline CTA keeping small buttons sized to their labels.
findings.reference: The competitor's inline CTA (product_manufacturer 13) keeps its two black buttons small on phones. They sit side by side under the text, each sized to its one-line label, with an 8px radius and 12px 24px padding.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, leave the @media (max-width: 767px) `.block--cta .cta .button { width: 100% }` rule in place for the band and form variants, and add an override for the inline variant after it: `@media (max-width: 767px) { .block--cta[data-variant="inline"] .cta .button { width: auto; max-width: 100%; padding-inline: 1.5rem; } }`. The button then fits its label and starts on the left edge under the paragraph.

findings.issue: The line joining the circles is still drawn only along the first row, and it runs past the last circle (03) to the content's right edge in both samples, while the six-step sample's second row (04–06) has no line, so one sequence looks like two different treatments (raised in the last review and still not fixed).
findings.reference: The competitor's step rows (the timeline row on navy) draw one continuous thin line across the steps of their own row, and the line ends at the last step.
findings.fix: In the shared process:circles CSS, draw the line per step: a `::after` on each step's marker running to the next marker in the same row, left off each row's last step, in place of the single line under the list's first row.

findings.issue: On phones the longest sample's heading ('OEM Bikini Sampling, / Lead Times, Payment / and Shipping') still wraps to three lines at line-height 1, so each line's descenders nearly touch the capitals below and the heading reads as a cramped block (raised in the last review; `.block h2 { line-height: 1; }` is unchanged).
findings.reference: The competitor gives its headings that run over several lines clear spacing between lines: the hero headline at 88/96.8px (1.1) and section h2s at 60/84px (1.4).
findings.fix: In reference.css, raise `.block h2 { line-height: 1; }` to about 1.15–1.2, as `.page-hero h1` has at 1.15; leave the size and the fit variables to the template.

findings.issue: The section heading 'What Drives Your Fabric Cost' is still set in heavy bold (DM Sans 700) at both widths, while the competitor's matching intro/proof heading ('Your Collection, Kept On Track') is a light, regular-weight display line. This repeats the earlier finding: reference.css has no `.block--proof h2` weight rule, and the shots still show the bold heading.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its intro/proof heading large and light (regular or book weight), and uses bold only for short phrases inside the body text ('product development coordinator', 'we care about your brand as much as you do').
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `.block--proof[data-variant="band"] h2 { font-weight: 500; }` (or 400). Leave its size to the template's fit.

findings.issue: At 390px the three-column fabric table wraps most cells to one or two words a line ('Standard / spandex / blends', 'LYCRA Xtra / Life, / Carvico, / ECONYL, / REPREVE', 'Relative / price'), so rows run three to five lines high. The earlier finding asked for less panel padding, but the panel's inset is already small; the space goes to the cell padding and the full-size body type in three columns.
findings.reference: The competitor's intro/proof modules run their text in comfortable lines on phones, with no column squeezed to a word a line.
findings.fix: In reference.css, under 600px, set `.prose__table :is(th, td)` to an inline padding of about 0.375rem and the table's font-size to about 0.9375rem, so the two value columns get their width back and the header cells hold to two lines.

findings.issue: In the shortest sample the grey photo and the blush copy panel are two separate boxes with a white strip about 30 px wide between them, so the panel does not read as one blush block joined to its photo.
findings.reference: The competitor's sampling module (product_manufacturer 10) sets the blush copy panel directly against the photo, with no gap: one joined rectangle split into blush text and photo.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set `.block--split[data-variant="panel"] .split { column-gap: 0; }` so the photo and .split__copy meet. Keep the equal top and bottom edges and the copy centred on the photo's middle as they are.

findings.issue: On phones the photo stacks under the blush panel with a white strip about 25 px tall between them, although the panel and photo already run to the band's edges as one unit.
findings.reference: The competitor's panel and photo touch, with no gap between the blush panel and the photo.
findings.fix: In the existing `@media (max-width: 899px)` rule for `.block--split[data-variant="panel"] .split`, add `row-gap: 0` so the stacked photo meets the panel's lower edge.

findings.issue: The longest sample (/rash-guard-manufacturer/) has no photo, so the blush panel spans the whole content width with its copy in the left 60% and an empty blush area of about 40% on the right, which reads as a missing image.
findings.reference: The competitor's panel module always pairs the blush copy half with a photo half; there is no copy-only panel.
findings.fix: Have Site Factory supply the photo for block m7 on /rash-guard-manufacturer/, so the split renders the photo and panel side by side like the shortest sample.

findings.issue: The line that opens the section, 'How size-by-size print placement works', is the block's lead with no heading above it, so it renders at body size and regular weight. That makes it smaller and lighter than the bold card titles under it, and the section reads upside down. m7-steps' 'Care steps from our rash guard labels.' has the same problem at both widths. The earlier review sent this to content, but reference.css already has a rule for leads without a heading (lines 366–367); it covers the list and timeline variants and leaves out photo-cards.
findings.reference: The competitor opens its sections with a bold heading above the cards, heavier than the card titles.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process:not(:has(> .process__heading)) > .block__lead` to the selector at lines 366–367. That sets the lead in the heading face at --size-card-heading, at the heading weight, in --heading-color (white here).

findings.issue: The earlier review asked for wider side padding, and it is still not applied. Each card keeps about 20px on each side (card 01: outline at x 434, text at x 455), against about 40px above the title under the number badge, so titles and text sit close to the white outline. The desktop cards show the same, in both blocks.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards pad their content evenly on every side, about 32px.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `padding-inline: 2rem` on `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step` (patterns.css:605 still sets 1.25rem). Move the `.process-step__marker` left offset to the same 2rem so the badge stays over the title's edge.

findings.issue: Each stacked card still has about 50px of empty space under its last line, against about 40px above the title, so every card looks bottom-heavy. For example, card 01 ends its text near y 640 and its outline near y 690. This was reported before and the shots show it unchanged; m3-steps' cards show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards use the same padding on every side, so the content sits evenly inside the outline.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `margin-bottom: 0` on `.block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step > :last-child`, so the card's own bottom padding (1.5rem) is the only space under the text.

findings.issue: Still not fixed from the last review: the splitMedia:wide body paragraphs still run about 800 px at body size, close to 100 characters a line ('customisable development, production and worldwide delivery, and on to after-sales support. We've'), well past the ~70ch measure, while only the lead keeps to a short line; the existing 70ch cap in reference.css (main[data-authoring-page] .block p) does not reach this row as the board renders it.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps running text in short columns of about 60–75 characters, and treatment-practice.md holds running text to about 70ch at every width.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add the cap to the split row's own copy (e.g. .block--split .split__copy p { max-width: 68ch; }) so it applies wherever the module renders, not only under main[data-authoring-page]; leave the heading and the full-width photo as they are.

findings.issue: On phones the wide row's photo, stacked under about 750 px of copy, stays the desktop's shallow strip (about 350 × 153 px, roughly 2.3:1). It reads as a thin band rather than a photo, because the phone rule meant to give it its own shape (reference.css, comment 'Phones: the wide row's photo … shows in its own shape') has an empty body.
findings.reference: The competitor's photos beside text keep a full photo shape on phones (about 4:3 to 3:2), not a strip cut for a 1440 px row.
findings.fix: Fill the empty @media (max-width: 767px) block in src/styles/reference.css with an aspect-ratio of about 4/3 on the wide variant's media frame (e.g. .block--split[data-variant="wide"] .split__media { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; } with object-fit: cover on its img), or delete the empty block and its comment if the strip is intended.

findings.issue: The band still has no heading: a body-size lead ("Our full-package service, from brief to shipment.") sits directly above the steps, so the section has no title at either width.
findings.reference: The competitor's band opens with an eyebrow ("HOW IT WORKS") and a large H2 ("Six steps from Costing to delivery") above the rule that leads into the steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give this process block a heading (e.g. "Seven steps from brief to shipment") so h2.process__heading renders above the lead.

findings.issue: The band still has neither a heading nor a lead. Five bare steps start under an empty band of top padding (also on phones, about 100 px before the first rule), so the dark section has no visible purpose.
findings.reference: The competitor's band always opens with an eyebrow and an H2 naming the process before the numbered steps.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give faq-steps a heading (e.g. "How a consulting project runs") and, if it has one, a short lead.

findings.issue: The step numbers are still white like the body text, and the band's rule still runs level with the first row's numbers (patterns.css .process-steps::before, top: 22px) rather than above them. The second row (05–07) has no rule at all, so the numbers do not read as an accent and the two rows are styled differently.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its step numbers ("01"–"06") small, bold and in its light-blue accent, a clear space below one full-width rule that sits under the heading and above every step.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set --process-marker-text on .block--process[data-variant="band"] to the light accent (the button's cyan). For min-width 768px, move the band's .process-steps::before to top: 0 with left/right: 0, and give .process-steps padding-top (about 2rem) so the one rule stands above both rows of numbers.

findings.issue: This is still unfixed from the last review. The heading 'A recent order' starts on the content's left edge, but in both samples the case cards are a narrow stack of about 46rem centred in the column. The cards start about 330px right of the heading, leaving an empty band on the left and about a third of the width empty on the right, so the heading and cards share no edge.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each section's heading, text and cards in one column from the same left edge. It never pairs a left-set heading with a centred block of content. Its outlined cards (1px #979797, radius 6–10px) sit in the content grid, never as a floating centred stack.
findings.fix: In the template's src/styles/patterns.css, give `.order-cases` `margin-inline: 0` instead of `auto` when body[data-heading-align="start"] is set. The stack then starts on the heading's edge, and max-width stays only as the line-length limit. Alternatively, let the stack fill the content width as an equal-column grid with the cards side by side.

findings.issue: This is still unfixed from the last review. The same three-word heading 'A recent order' renders at about 60px in the longest sample and about 40px in the shortest, so the same heading in the same module gets a different size depending on how much body copy the block has.
findings.reference: The competitor uses one size per heading level in every section, so a section heading looks the same wherever it appears.
findings.fix: Make the template's heading fit for the orderCase heading depend only on the heading's own words, so identical headings get the same size whatever the length of the block's body copy. Change only the fit logic; add no font-size rule.

findings.issue: This repeats an earlier finding that the shots still show: the bars run the full content width (about 1400px), so one-line questions stop halfway across and the +/− sits several hundred pixels away from its question. The open answer also wraps at about half that width, so the question and its answer don't share a measure.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps its bars in a narrower column. Question, marker and answer read as one bar, and the answer runs nearly the bar's full width.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give the item list of .block--faq[data-variant="bars"] a max-width in ch sized to the longest question (about 90–100ch), left-aligned under the heading. Let the answer fill that bar. This is a reading measure, not the competitor's pixel width.

findings.issue: This repeats an earlier finding that the shots still show: the open/close mark is a +/− at the far right end of each bar, not a marker before the question.
findings.reference: The competitor puts a small solid triangle (▸, turning ▾ when open) just before the question text, at the left of each bar.
findings.fix: Give the template a marker option for faq[data-variant="bars"] that puts a triangle before the summary text, in place of the shared ::after +/− at the right.

findings.issue: This repeats an earlier finding that the shots still show: on phones each bar's track fills only about half the panel, and the value ("4 cm", "7 cm") sits at the far right with an empty gap between bar and figure.
findings.reference: On desktop the same chart's track fills the width between label and value, so bar and figure stay together.
findings.fix: At narrow widths, let the .charts bar track grow (flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0) to fill the row up to the value.

findings.issue: On phones the comparison table (shortest sample) is wider than its panel. The third column ("Pigment with white underlayer") is cut off at the right edge as "Pigm / with / und", and the only sign that the table scrolls sideways is a thin scrollbar sliver.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ module carries no wide table. Its content keeps to the panel width on phones.
findings.fix: In the shared charts/table component, stack the table on narrow widths: each column becomes a labelled card, or each row a label above its values. Failing that, add a visible sideways-scroll cue (an edge fade and a 'scroll' hint) to the table wrapper.

findings.issue: The consent line still reads 'I agree that my details are used to answer this enquiry, as described in the privacy policy.' and then repeats 'Privacy policy' as a separate link on its own indented second line.
findings.reference: The competitor's form has no repeated text under its fields. The only thing below its message box is the dark SEND bar.
findings.fix: In LeadForm.astro, turn the words 'privacy policy' inside consent.label into the link, and stop adding a second 'Privacy policy' link after the label.

findings.issue: This was reported before and is still not fixed: on phones the four channel cards stack one per row at full width. Each card is a tall, mostly empty box holding one small icon, an oversized label bar (1.25rem bold) and one line of text, so the section runs to about 880 px. The cause is reference.css line 483, `@media (max-width: 599px) { .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] > .contact-channel { flex-basis: 100%; } }`.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps its channel cards as compact outlined tiles on phones, two by two (components.md, contact section 3; the mobile shot shows the four tiles side by side). Each tile has an icon over a black label bar.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css line 483, change flex-basis: 100% to flex-basis: calc(50% - var(--grid-gap) / 2) with min-width: 0 so the cards sit two by two. Add overflow-wrap: anywhere to the card's value text so the email address breaks inside a half-width card. Below 600px, bring .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] .contact-channel__name down to about 1rem with 0.375rem 0.75rem padding so the label bar fits the smaller tile.

findings.issue: This was reported before and is still not fixed: the parts of the cards in the one row do not line up. The email and phone links sit about 5 px lower under their label bars than the plain address and hours text (y≈200 against y≈195 on the shot).
findings.reference: The competitor's channel cards put their icon, label bar and text at the same heights across the row.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, give the linked value (a[href]) and the plain-text value inside .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] .contact-channel the same box: the same display, line-height, padding and margin, with no extra block padding or min-height on the link. Then the line under every label bar starts at one height.

findings.issue: The channel icons are small, thin line glyphs, about 24 px across, floating in the card's top band. The icon reads much weaker than the black label bar under it, and the top of each card looks empty.
findings.reference: The competitor's channel cards lead with a large icon, about 60–70 px across and often set in a round badge, centred above the label bar, so the icon carries the card.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, raise --channel-icon-size (and --channel-icon-box) for .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] to about 2.5rem on desktop. Keep the line-icon style and stroke colour; on phones, the box can keep following the icon size as it does now.

findings.issue: The process:timeline steps still have no step number or marker: each row is a bold label beside its text over a hairline, so the six steps read as a definitions table, not an ordered sequence (the same at 390 px, where the labels stack over their text with nothing to count them).
findings.reference: Every competitor step module numbers its steps: blue '01–03' numerals on the three-step process, and a number over each title and text above a hairline on the six-step navy timeline (components.md). This site's own process list variant already does this with its 01/02/03 counter.
findings.fix: In ProcessBlock.astro, render the step number (number(index), as the list and photo-cards variants already do) as a .process-step__marker before each .process-timeline__label, in the accent colour; in patterns.css, make room for it in the label column (on phones, beside the label).

findings.issue: Because the fit sizes the heading to its words across the full content width, the section heading 'What to Send for a Free, Accurate Quotation' is set at page-title size (about 64 px, about 2.5× the 26 px heading of m8-steps of the same module) and runs well past the right edge of its own timeline rows and lead, so the module's heading and body don't share a width.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its section headings well below its page titles, one size for each heading level, and keeps each heading inside its module's column.
findings.fix: In the template's heading fit, cap a section h2's fitted size at the h2 step (below the page title's fitted size) and fit it to the module's own measure (the .process-timeline width) instead of the full content width.

findings.issue: This is still open from the last review: all ten cards repeat the same grey label 'What this means for you' between the title and the text. It is the cards' only row label, so it adds a filler line to every card at both widths (on phones it adds one line of height to each of ten cards stacked in one column).
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards have just a bold title and their text, with no repeated field label (components.md: three outlined cards, title 700, text below).
findings.fix: In TableBlock.astro's cards layout, leave out the dt column label when the table has only one data column (or make it visually hidden for screen readers), and render the cell as the card's paragraph directly under .table-card__title.
